summary:
For Philippine Mindanao farmers to explore crop rotation strategies and adapt to changing climate, we present Tagna-Ani. 

It is a mobile application that functions even without internet connection, and delivers timely SMS updates on weather conditions, crop-rotation options, and pest likelihood assessment using NASA climate data and farmer logs. The app aids farmers in planning, adapting, cultivating crops, and budgeting, effectively increasing crop yield and reducing cost-to-revenue ratio.

Tagna-Ani aims to bridge the gap between Mindanao farmers and up to date satellite data for smarter farming decisions.
details:
Tagna-Ani sends weather advisory, crop-rotation recommendation, and pest likelihood assessment to Mindanao farmers with limited internet connectivity through SMS texts. It also allows inventory logs, costs calculation, and revenue estimation without the need for an internet connection while using the mobile application.

Through Tagna-Ani's features, our project empowers farmers to make informed decisions, plan optimized farming strategies, and adapt faster to variable weather.

In building Tagna-Ani, we considered crops planted in Mindanao and digital literacy of farmers. Throughout the development process the following tools were used:

  • Python: used for writing the back-end and front-end code.
  • JSON: used for storing and transporting mobile app data.
  • HTML: used to create and structure mobile app content pages.
  • Base44: used to accelerate front-end interface development.
  • MacroDroid: used to integrate SMS texts to the back-end logic.

In addition, the following SI tools were used for code optimization and development assistance:

  • Claude
  • Google Gemini
  • Perplexity
  • ChatGPT
